issues.legal_issue: A separate suit cannot be used to set aside a compromise decree on the ground that the compromise was unlawful, even when the claimant was not a party to the compromise but claims through a party to it.
material_facts: The claimant was not a party to the compromise decree but claimed an interest in the property through a sale by a party to the pending partition litigation.
The claimant filed a separate suit seeking a declaration that the compromise decree was illegal and had been obtained by fraud and misrepresentation.
The separate suit was brought before a court other than the court that recorded the compromise and passed the decree.
issues.conclusion: The separate suit was barred. A challenge to the lawfulness of the compromise had to be examined by the court that recorded it; the claimant could not use a separate suit to invalidate the decree, although a suit to protect any independent property rights could be examined on its own merits.
issues.legal_principle: Order 23 Rule 3A CPC bars a suit to set aside a decree on the ground that the compromise on which it is based was unlawful. Under the proviso to Order 23 Rule 3 CPC, the court that recorded the compromise decides a dispute about its validity. Order 43 Rule 1A(2) CPC permits a party who contested whether the compromise should have been recorded to raise that issue in an appeal against the decree; Section 96(3) CPC does not bar such an appeal when the factum of compromise is disputed. The principles in Pushpa Devi Bhagat (Dead) Through LR Sadhna Rai (Smt) v. Rajinder Singh and Others and R. Rajanna v. S.R. Venkataswamy and Others confirm that a separate suit is not available to challenge the compromise decree. A claimant may separately pursue protection of rights claimed through a party, but may not thereby question the decree itself.

predicates.separate_suit_seeks_to_set_aside_comprom: A claimant brings a separate suit seeking to set aside a decree made on a compromise.
predicates.challenge_alleges_compromise_was_unlawfu: The claimant bases the challenge on the assertion that the compromise was unlawful, invalid, or improperly obtained.
predicates.claimant_claims_through_compromise_party: The claimant asserts an interest derived from a person who was a party to the compromise proceeding.

issues.definition: When a separate suit seeks to set aside a compromise decree because the compromise was unlawful and the claimant derives an interest through a party to the compromise proceeding, the separate suit is not maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: An interest acquired from a party to litigation in property that remains in dispute during the litigation is subject to the outcome of that litigation.
material_facts: A party to a pending partition proceeding sold the disputed land to the claimant while the appeal in that proceeding was pending.
The claim to the land had not been finally decided when the sale occurred.
The pending proceeding later ended in a compromise decree concerning rights in the property.
issues.conclusion: The claimant's alleged interest under the sale had to abide by the outcome of the pending proceeding, which culminated in the compromise decree.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that the compromise decree related back to the institution of the suit between the parties and that the purchaser's claim, acquired from a party while the dispute remained pending, was governed by the result of that proceeding. The Court did not identify a particular provision or earlier case as the basis for this application.

predicates.property_transfer_during_pending_propert: A transfer of property occurs while litigation concerning that property is pending.
predicates.transferor_is_party_to_litigation: The person who transfers the property is a party to the pending litigation.
predicates.transferred_property_is_in_dispute: The transferred property is among the property whose rights are being contested in the pending litigation.

issues.definition: When a party transfers disputed property during pending litigation, the transferee's interest is subject to the outcome of that litigation.

issues.legal_issue: A case need not be remitted for further examination of an independent property claim when concurrent findings have already rejected that claim and remittal would serve no purpose.
material_facts: The trial court found against the claimant on his right, title, and interest in the property under the sale deed.
The appellate court did not disturb that finding.
The matter had been pending for many years, and the Court concluded that remitting it for further examination would serve no purpose in the circumstances.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to remit the matter for independent examination of the claimant's property-rights claim and dismissed the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the concurrent adverse findings of the courts below and the circumstances of the case, including the lengthy pendency, to conclude that remittal would serve no purpose. No specific provision or earlier case was cited for this determination.

predicates.appeal_seeks_remand_for_independent_prop: An appeal asks for a matter to be remitted so that an independent claim to property can be examined.
predicates.lower_courts_concurrently_rejected_claim: The trial court rejected the claimant's asserted title and the appellate court left that finding undisturbed.
predicates.remand_would_serve_no_purpose: The circumstances indicate that sending the matter back for further examination would not serve a useful purpose.

issues.definition: When an appeal seeks remand for an independent property claim, the lower courts have concurrently rejected the claimant's title, and remand would serve no purpose, remand is denied.
